common_thread.question: What keeps showing up across your established heroes?
common_thread.question_body: Choose the functional job you think keeps recurring, then compare it with the evidence-backed read.
common_thread.correct_feedback: Yes — {trait} is the strongest recurring thread across the established pool.
common_thread.incorrect_feedback: {selected} shows up in the pool, but {trait} has the stronger cross-hero coverage.
common_thread.answer: A common functional thread runs through the pool: {trait}.
common_thread.reveal: {trait} is the strongest recurring functional trait across {hero_count} established heroes.
common_thread.boundary: This describes what the heroes tend to offer; it does not prove those tools were used correctly in every match.

exception.question: Which hero gives your pool a different kind of Dota?
exception.question_body: Pick the hero you expect to break the pool's usual functional shape.
exception.incorrect: Good guess — but not this one.
exception.correct_feedback: Yes — {hero} breaks the pool's functional shape most clearly.
exception.incorrect_feedback: {selected} fits the pool's core shape more closely. {hero} breaks it more clearly.
exception.no_clear_feedback: {selected} is a plausible read, but the evidence does not separate one exception cleanly.
exception.answer: {hero} is the clearest functional outlier in this pool.
exception.reveal: {hero} breaks the pool’s usual functional shape more clearly than the alternatives.
exception.boundary: Different does not mean better or worse.

evolution.question: How do you think your hero pool has changed recently?
evolution.question_body: Choose the description that feels closest. This is a self-assessment, not a score.
evolution.unavailable: The bounded history could not support a trustworthy Pool Evolution comparison yet.
evolution.locked: Complete the self-assessment above to see the report read.
evolution.option_same_style: My heroes changed, but my style didn’t
evolution.option_different_kind: I’ve shifted toward a different kind of hero
evolution.new_heroes_new_toolkit: Your pool changed direction. The names are not the only thing changing. The kind of Dota available in your pool is changing too.
evolution.new_heroes_same_toolkit: New heroes. Same taste. Your recent picks look different, but the jobs you keep asking your heroes to perform barely moved.
evolution.stable_core_new_branch: Your pool is growing a new branch. Your familiar core is still intact, but a different kind of hero is beginning to appear more often.
evolution.broadly_stable: More stable than it feels. The edges moved a little, but the core hero mix and the kinds of jobs it covers stayed broadly recognizable.

hero_mirror.closed: One last comparison: your observable behavior against a hero-shaped reference.
hero_mirror.available: Of the heroes you've played enough for us to trust, {hero} is where your usual Dota shows up most clearly.
hero_mirror.unavailable: The current history does not support a stable Hero Mirror yet.
hero_mirror.qualifier: Not your best hero. Not necessarily your most played.
hero_mirror.guardrail: This is not a personality test. We're not saying you are {hero}. We're saying your games on {hero} most closely resemble the way you usually play Dota.

element.observation: {label} landed in the {zone} zone across the bounded summary history.
element.distinctive: It was selected as one of the clearest signals in this report.
element.evidence: The receipt below shows the summary fields supporting this signal.
element.notice: Notice the zone and the sample together; neither is a verdict.
element.guardrail: This describes an observed pattern, not why it happened.

pattern.worth_noticing: The relationship is visible in the Element zones below.
pattern.player_read: This relationship describes how the signals moved together; it does not claim a cause.
pattern.takeaway: Keep an eye on whether the same relationship appears in another window.
pattern.guardrail: The result is bounded by the summary fields and the required Element evidence.

pattern_action.same_playbook_heading: Where do you want to take this?
pattern_action.same_playbook_intro: Both directions are valid: keep solving the same kind of Dota problem, or add range without abandoning your anchors.
pattern_action.same_playbook_deepen_description: More heroes that keep your current game familiar.
pattern_action.same_playbook_stretch_description: Bridge heroes that add a new answer while preserving an anchor.
pattern_action.same_playbook_empty_direction: No candidate cleared the evidence and learning-distance gates for this direction.
pattern_action.comfort_edge_kicker: Build the pool with a reason
pattern_action.comfort_edge_heading: Your strongest heroes are the safest part of this pool today.
pattern_action.comfort_edge_intro: Here is why the other established heroes can still be worth learning. This is a player-relative reliability read, not a meta ranking.
